tools/perf/ is the first subdirectory under tools/ — _discover_repo_modules() only globs tools/*.py non-recursively, so modules here aren't registered as repo module stems and the test file's bare `import replay_bench`/`import trace_from_telemetry` (via manual sys.path insertion, not `from tools.perf.X import`) never lands in the import graph either. Without this entry, an edit to either file gets a fast-CI subset that silently omits its own test, with no fail-open backstop (found by the reviewer-fairy on PR #1676).

The checker reports an ABSENCE (no bash-4-only constructs in shipped shell scripts), and an absence-reporting tool is trustworthy only if its detector demonstrably fires on a positive. The mapped suite therefore weights the detector's falsifiability — every pattern matches a known-positive AND rejects the portable bash-3.2 equivalent — over its plumbing. The hyphenated filename means it is loaded by path, not imported, so it has no import-graph edge and would otherwise be layer-1-unreachable.
